Name: The Infinity Tones - Skin Tone Color Picker
Author: Spiderbuttons
Description:
[b][size=4]Installation[/size][/b]
[list]
[*][url=https://smapi.io]Install the latest version of SMAPI[/url].[/*]
[*]Extract the mod into Stardew Valley/Mods.[/*]
[*]Run the game using SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]The vanilla game only comes with 24 different skin tones you can choose from, and that's awfully limiting. Real life doesn't choose from only 24 different skin tones. You can install skin tone mods, but up until now these have also just been limited to a [i]different[/i] set of 24 skin tones, and if you don't like the ones the mod author chose, you're out of luck. And good luck if you wanted to play with a friend who wanted a different set of skin tones.

[b][size=4]The Infinity Tones works differently from the other skin tone mods out there.[/size][/b] This mod lets you choose [i]any[/i] colour to use as your skin tone during character customization. I mean it, ANY colour. You can open up a standard colour picker and choose the precise colour you want for your skin and have it applied to your character. You don't HAVE to choose a custom skin tone, you can still select from the ordinary 24 built-in skin tones if you want, but if you DO want a custom skin tone, here's what that looks like:

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/51901/51901-1788817610-77025967.png[/img]

As you can see, the only limit to what colours you can choose are your imagination. And what computers are capable of displaying. You can see in the screenshot that not only can you select the base [b]Tone[/b] of your skin, but also adjust the [b]Shading[/b] and [b]Outline[/b] colours as well. There's no reason these NEED to be of a similar colour to your main skin tone. You can be a bright blue farmer with orange shading and a neon pink outline if you really want. Just click on whichever one you want to edit and adjust to your liking. The preview on the left side will show you the results.

[b]Auto Palette[/b] is there to make things easier if you don't care to be super specific about your shading and outline, though. Turning that on will mean you can only edit the Tone colour, but both the Shading and Outline colours will automatically adjust to match. If you're not happy with their auto-generated colours, you can always turn off Auto Palette again after to do some fine-tuning.

The [b]Dark Skin[/b] toggle is there to let you determine whether or not your skin tone is considered "dark" skin, for the purposes of in-game child genetics. If you plan to have a child with the NPC you eventually marry, checking the Dark Skin box means that your farmer will contribute to the chance for your baby to be born with dark skin. If the box is not checked, your farmer will be considered as not having dark skin and thus your baby will only have a chance to have dark skin if the NPC you marry is considered by the game to have dark skin. At this time, babies do not inherit custom skin tones (but they don't in vanilla either, they are limited to just [i]two[/i] skin tones. Maybe in a future update I'll change this, too.)

Beneath the colour picker, you'll see the coloured box labeled "[b]Vanilla Skin Tone[/b]." When you choose a custom skin tone with this mod, it will automatically find the closest matching vanilla skin tone for you and apply it to your farmer behind the scenes, beneath your custom skin tone. What this means is that if you ever uninstall this mod, your farmer will be left with the skin tone that it shows in the "Vanilla Skin Tone" box. This way, uninstalling this mod will at least leave your skin tone at a colour as close as possible to what you originally intended. You can always go back to the Wizard to change your skin again if you're still not happy with it.

Speaking of the wizard, this mod works when you go to his character customizer too. So if you've already started a farm and want a custom skin tone, you can go to his basement and change your skin tone there. You'll have access to the same colour picker and all the same options within.

[size=6][b]Does this work with Fashion Sense?[/b][/size]
Yes!* This mod [b]fully supports Fashion Sense[/b] and is 100% compatible with it! Any clothing or accessories you wear will show your custom skin tone from this mod. The only times it won't are when you are wearing an outfit or Fashion Sense body type that is supposed to override your body colour. In those cases, you can set the colour with Fashion Sense as normal.

[size=5][b]Does this work with my body mod?[/b][/size]
Yes! This mod supports every standard body mod right out of the gate. Your custom body mod will show your custom skin tone that you selected with this mod, even if that body mod itself came with its own set of skin tones.

[size=5][b]Does this work with multiplayer?[/b][/size]
Yes!* This mod fully supports both split screen and online multiplayer. Farmhands will be able to select a custom skin tone when they create their character, just like the host can, and every player will see every other player with the correct custom skin tone that they chose, as long as everyone has this mod installed. If someone does not have this mod installed, they will see people with whatever Vanilla Skin Tone was chosen for them.

[size=5][b]Does this work with my skin tone mod?[/b][/size]
Yes technically! While there's no reason to have both a skin tone palette mod installed alongside this mod, it won't break anything if you do. If you choose a custom skin tone with this mod, it will override the skin tones from your skin tone palette mod. You can still select from the 24 built-in skin tones like you would normally with a skin tone palette mod if you want, and ignore this mod entirely, but it comes with the downsides of not being multiplayer friendly anymore. Also, the Vanilla Skin Tone feature mentioned above only matches to the actual vanilla, unmodded skin tones, not those added by your skin tone mod. Again though, there's no reason to have a skin tone mod installed alongside this one! Whatever colours are in your skin tone mod, you can just choose them within this mod's colour picker.

[size=5][b]Will my children have the same skin tone?[/b][/size]
No! Like vanilla, children are still limited to one of two preset skin tones and do not inherit your custom skin tone. The odds of your child having dark skin are determined by whether or not you selected the "Dark Skin" checkbox when choosing your custom skin tone and whether or not the NPC you married has what the game considers to be a dark skin tone. It's possible that I may in the future add the ability for children to inherit your skin tone, but it's not currently planned due to compatibility concerns.

[b][size=5]Do I need to start a new save file to use this?[/size][/b]
No! Just go to the Wizard and change your skin there, or use the "debug cmenu" console command in your SMAPI console.

[b][size=5]Does this have controller support?[/size][/b]
Yes! The entire colour picker menu fully supports controllers.

[b][size=5]Is this safe to uninstall?[/size][/b]
Yes! The only permanent change this mod makes to your character is what skin tone the game thinks you have. When you uninstall this mod, your skin tone will be set to whatever the Vanilla Skin Tone in the colour picker menu was, which is the closest match to the vanilla skin tones that my mod could find. You can always go to the Wizard and change your skin there or use the "debug cmenu" console command in your SMAPI console if you're not happy with the selection.

If you ever reinstall the mod later on, your previous custom skin tone will be restored, as it gets saved into your save file even when the mod is not uninstalled. It won't do anything without this mod installed though, of course.
[line]
*If a player [b]in multiplayer[/b] changes their skin tone in the middle of the game, some Fashion Sense accessories may not update their colour correctly for other players until the game is relaunched. This is actually a Fashion Sense bug that would happen with or without this mod installed. Before reporting any bugs to me relating to Fashion Sense, please confirm first whether or not the same kind of bug still happens even if you uninstall my mod.
